## Plan-review on this epic BLOCKED, which blocks its children from being claimed

`rebar review-plan 0480-df66-b3df-4aee` returned **BLOCK** (1 blocking, 8 advisory):

> AC6 requires re-taking measurements 'after change 2685 deploys', but the plan states 2685 is
> NOT DEPLOYED; if the deploy is not operator-scheduled this session, AC6 cannot be completed
> in-session.

The finding is correct as written. This matters beyond the epic itself because of the
**parent-first claim cascade**: a child cannot be claimed while its parent is `open` and
unclaimable, so `rebar claim 48f0-f7ff-c8df-43ac` (`cryptozoic-unlit-ladybug`) fails with

    cannot claim 48f0-...: its parent 0480-... could not be claimed first

even though that child holds its OWN certified, passing plan-review attestation
(`verified_at_sha ca89152f7b3ff02178352de3db13a3fad9a56fbc`).

**I have not edited this epic and have not used any force override.** Changing AC6 would be
altering the acceptance bar of work I do not own, and doing it to unblock myself is precisely
the accommodation-instead-of-fix pattern this epic's "Negative recommendation" section
forbids. Two resolutions are available to whoever owns this epic, both non-bypassing:

1. Reword AC6 so it is satisfiable independently of a deploy this session — e.g. "the
   measurements are re-taken and recorded once 2685 deploys" as a recorded follow-up rather
   than an in-session completion condition, or split it into its own child ticket.
2. Some other rework that clears the finding, then `review-plan` again and move the epic to
   `in_progress`.

Either unblocks every child, not just this one.

## AC6 discharged: change 2685 is deployed, and the measurements are re-taken

AC6 held this epic (and, via the parent-first claim cascade, every child) because the 4.45 GB MCP
figure predated the projection fix and could not be trusted. Both halves are now satisfied.

### 2685 is deployed — proven, not assumed

```
Gerrit 2685  "Reduce discovery reads without the bodies"   status MERGED
             submitted 2026-09-05 22:29:25   rebar-ticket: 9ea3-7d07-ea55-4496
             merged as 1bffbd586a25

running MCP container:  rebar-mcp-8e14d667da28-8092      (autodeploy names it for its commit)
git merge-base --is-ancestor 1bffbd586a25 8e14d667da28  ->  TRUE
```

The container in service is built from `8e14d667`, and 2685's commit is an ancestor of it. So the
running MCP **contains** the projection fix. This matters because "merged" is not "deployed" on this
host — the nginx edge proved that earlier tonight, where a merged change sat inert because that
surface is detect-only under autodeploy. Here the container name carries its own commit, which is
what makes the deployment checkable rather than inferred.

### Re-taken measurements (2026-09-06 01:29 UTC, post-deploy)

```
free -m:   total 7813   used 4796   free 564   buff/cache 2453   available 2615   (33.5%)
uptime:    load average 4.69, 4.99, 5.08      <-- 2 vCPU, ~2.5x oversubscribed
df -h /:   60G total, 42G used, 19G free (69%)

docker stats --no-stream:
  rebar-mcp-8e14d667da28-8092   2.872GiB / 7.631GiB   37.64%
  compose-review-bot-1           628.6MiB / 7.631GiB    8.05%
  compose-gerrit-1               639.1MiB / 7.631GiB    8.18%
  compose-opcert-1                40.55MiB / 7.631GiB    0.52%
```

**The old figure was substantially wrong, exactly as AC6 suspected — and wrong in the helpful
direction.** MCP measures **2.87 GiB**, not 4.45 GB. AC6 was right to refuse to let the plan rest on
it.

Two corrections to figures used elsewhere in this epic's discussion: host total is **7,813 MiB, not
7,987**, and there is **no ~0.97 GB quiet MCP baseline** — it sits at 2.2-2.9 GiB.

### What the corrected numbers change, and what they do not

They do **not** dissolve the problem. Sizing each service for measured steady state plus one
concurrent gate still does not fit:

```
gerrit 3072 + mcp 3655 + review-bot 1343 + opcert 256  =  8326 MiB   against a 7813 MiB host
```

Over by **513 MiB before any OS headroom**, with MCP's steady state alone at 38% of the box. That
arithmetic is now based on post-2685 measurements, so it is evidence rather than an artifact of the
stale figure.

They also **confirm the concurrency bound**. Against 2,615 MiB available: 4 permitted plan-reviews
need ~2,856 MiB and exhaust memory; 2 need ~1,428 MiB, leaving 1,187 MiB — just above the 1,024 MiB
admission floor, so a third is refused by the floor anyway. The count and the floor are
complementary rather than redundant.

### One finding that changes how the limits must be applied

A compose `mem_limit` on the `mcp:` service **would never have bound the running container.**
`mcp_run_new()` at `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:654` is a bare `docker run -d` whose own comment says
compose never sees it. `docker ps` confirms it independently: MCP is named
`rebar-mcp-<sha>-8092` by that function, while the other three are `compose-<service>-1`. The bound
must be `--memory` on that `docker run`, pinned to compose by the existing parity oracle
`test_docker_run_matches_compose_mcp_service`. Note also that every container reports the **host
total** (`7.631GiB`) as its limit today — empirical proof that none is currently bounded.

Recording this here so the epic's own AC6 no longer blocks its children on a measurement that has
now been taken.

compiled_state.description:
# Stabilise the rebar service host: bound the SUM, separate the batch tier

## The thesis

The Gerrit host is not suffering a series of unrelated bugs. It is **oversubscribed, with nothing
enforcing the total**, and the individual failures are symptoms of contention.

```
instance                t4g.large — 2 vCPU, 7.8 GiB, 30% CPU baseline
rebar-mcp               4.45 GB RSS   (measured 2026-09-05)
Gerrit JVM              ~2 GB heap pinned + overhead
                        ─────────────────────────────
resident before work    ~6.9 GB of 7.8 GiB   (89%)

max_concurrent_gates    4   (code default; [snapshot] absent from rebar.toml)
plan_review peak RSS    ~714 MB each   (measured GATE_PEAK_RSS)
4 concurrent gates      +2.8 GB
                        ─────────────────────────────
PERMITTED TOTAL         ~9.7 GB on a 7.8 GiB box

container memory limits DECLARED: NONE (docker-compose.yml has no mem_limit)
```

Permitted concurrency exceeds physical memory by ~2 GB. With no per-container limits the kernel
arbitrates by OOM-killing whatever it picks, which is why the host WEDGES rather than degrades,
why a soft reboot did not clear the 2026-09-05 outage, and why only a stop/start recovered it.

**This is the same defect already filed against `observability.sh`** (`ignitable-fuchsia-kawala`):
over 495 s of individually-defensible ceilings inside a 240 s timeout, each comment justifying
itself against the total, nothing summing them. Identical error one level up: every component has
a bound, nothing bounds the whole.

## Three workloads, three profiles, one box

- **Gerrit** — latency-sensitive, always-up, steady memory, CPU-bursty on packfile generation.
- **rebar MCP** — latency-sensitive, memory spiky in proportion to concurrency.
- **review-bot gates** — BATCH: 15-20 min, ~700 MB, queueable, bursty.

Co-locating a batch workload with two interactive services on a BURSTABLE instance is the design
error. Gates consume the CPU credits and page cache the interactive services need, and they are the
swing factor that takes memory over the line. Note the corollary the arithmetic forces: at current
resident usage the box cannot safely run even ONE plan-review gate. Tuning the semaphore from 4
downward does not reach a safe number — which is the argument for moving the tier, not retuning it.

## Workstreams, in leverage order

**W1 — Move gate execution off the Gerrit host.** Nothing requires co-location: a gate needs
network access to Gerrit, a clone, and an API key. Removes the bursty heavy consumer entirely; no
recurring cost. `Verified` already runs on GitHub runners.

**W2 — Declare per-container memory limits summing below RAM, with headroom.** Today there are
none. A limit converts "host wedges unpredictably" into "one container restarts, loudly" — a
bounded, observable failure. Requires W5's measurement to size correctly.

**W3 — Right-size or change instance family.** `CPUCreditBalance` has been 0.00 since 12:38Z with
`CPUSurplusCreditBalance` accruing (charged). Sustained demand above baseline means BURSTABLE IS
THE WRONG FAMILY, not a mistuned one. Operator decision — it costs money.

**W4 — Bound the SUM, not the parts.** One admission controller aware of total memory, replacing
independent gate semaphore + MCP thread limiter + review-bot concurrency, each locally reasonable.

**W5 — Telemetry that captures the RUN-UP.** Memory is the one major resource AWS does not publish
at hypervisor level, and our only memory signal comes from a probe that truncates. We do not need
telemetry that survives an outage; we need the twenty minutes before it.

## Negative recommendation — stop accommodating

Several changes landed or in review this session TUNE THRESHOLDS to accommodate starvation rather
than fix it: alarm windows 10 -> 30 min, `DOCKER_DU_TIMEOUT` 120 -> 60, `proxy_read_timeout`
60 -> 600 s. Each is defensible alone; together they teach the system to expect slowness and stop
reporting it. The alarm widening in change 2683 already carries an explicit revert trigger — narrow
it back once probe cadence is restored. **That revert must be honoured, not forgotten.**

Distinguish these from the session's genuine correctness fixes, which stand regardless of hardware:
`force_new_store` inert on the worktree path, `breaching` with M<N, the `pct_of_cap` clamp,
`is-ancestor` under rebase-on-submit, `user_data` over 16 KiB, nginx's missing directive,
`reduce_all_tickets` projecting after materialisation, `_scan_alias` scanning per resolve, and the
GC hanging inside its own lock.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 The sum of permitted concurrent memory demand is provably BELOW host RAM, with headroom,
      and something ENFORCES it rather than documenting it.
- [ ] AC2 A resource-exhaustion event degrades observably (a named container restarts, an admission
      is refused) instead of wedging the host. Demonstrated, not asserted.
- [ ] AC3 The batch gate tier no longer competes with Gerrit and MCP for the same RAM and CPU
      credits, OR a reasoned decision is recorded that it should.
- [ ] AC4 Host memory is measurable at a resolution that shows a 20-minute run-up, independent of
      the probe's truncation behaviour.
- [ ] AC5 The threshold widenings above are reverted once their preconditions land, or each is
      re-justified on its own merits with the starvation removed.
- [x] AC6 The measurements this plan rests on are re-taken after change 2685 deploys.
      **Discharged 2026-09-06.** 2685 (`1bffbd586a25`, "Reduce discovery reads without the
      bodies") merged 22:29:25 and IS deployed: the running container is
      `rebar-mcp-8e14d667da28-8092` and `git merge-base --is-ancestor 1bffbd586a25
      8e14d667da28` is true, so the MCP in service contains the projection fix. Post-deploy
      measurements taken 01:29 UTC are recorded in the comments. The 4.45 GB figure WAS
      substantially wrong, as this AC suspected: MCP measures **2.87 GiB**. Host total is
      **7,813 MiB** (not 7,987) and there is no ~0.97 GB quiet MCP baseline. The corrected
      numbers do not dissolve the problem -- per-service steady state plus one gate still
      sums to 8,326 MiB against 7,813 -- but that conclusion now rests on post-2685 data.

## What is NOT established

- Whether the 2026-09-05 outage was memory exhaustion. It fits every observation, and EBS burst,
  CPU saturation, hypervisor failure and disk pressure are all RULED OUT with data — but there is
  no memory series, so it is the leading candidate, not a finding (`retiring-coronary-muntjac`).
- Whether MCP's 4.45 GB is steady-state or accumulated allocator retention. Change 2685 cuts
  per-call cost 3.5x but is NOT DEPLOYED; the post-fix resident baseline is unmeasured.
- Actual peak concurrent gate count in practice versus the permitted 4.

## Constraints

Never use `--force` or any gate bypass. Terraform apply is operator-authorized this session and
must follow a reviewed plan. `timeout` does not exist on this macOS host (exit 127) — bound with
`perl -e 'alarm N; exec @ARGV'`. Do not touch the shared main checkout; do not `git stash`.

file_impact.reason: W2: no per-container memory limits declared today; the sum must be bounded below host RAM
W4: [snapshot].max_concurrent_gates is absent so the code default of 4 applies; 4x714MB exceeds available RAM
W3: instance family/size — burstable is wrong for sustained above-baseline demand
